question_record.context: A security incident was reported in which potentially compromised assets are exhibiting ransomware-like behavior, impacting several devices. An attacker may be operating using the specified user account, IP, or device to move laterally across the network and infect as many devices as possible with ransomware. The device involved in this alert is 'vnevado-win11t' with AadDeviceId 'e5799261-6720-4297-961e-bd9ca4275033'. Additionally, a file named 'characterical.zip.lockbit' was identified. A connected alert also indicated a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) used to enable single sign-on (SSO) across applications on different devices.
question_record.question: Can you identify the AadDeviceId of the host in which suspicious file system changes, indicative of ransomware activity, were detected?
solution: The user account `dp5hn` is potentially compromised and is exhibiting ransomware-like behavior.
There was a possible attempt to access the Primary Refresh Token (PRT) on the host with HostName `vnevado-win11u`.
Ransomware behavior was detected on the host with AadDeviceId `bc00e484-d0e5-4da4-9472-95568cccc07e`.

118.name: Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT)
118.description:
Possible attempt to access Primary Refresh Token (PRT) has been detected. A Primary Refresh Token (PRT) is a key artifact of Azure AD authentication on Windows 10, Windows Server 2016 and later versions, iOS, and Android devices. It is a JSON Web Token (JWT) that's specially issued to Microsoft first party token brokers to enable single sign-on (SSO) across the applications used on those devices. Attackers can attempt to access this resource to move laterally into organization or perform credential theft.

For more information, read the Activity profile: Midnight Blizzard credential attacks Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/e4aad043-a273-4f88-b65e-fdfc3996ec92/analystreport?

160.name: Ransomware behavior detected in the file system
160.description:
Suspicious file system changes might indicate ransomware activity. This potential ransomware activity might be indicative of mass encryption of files by ransomware.

For more information, read the Ransomware: A pervasive and ongoing threat Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/05658b6c-dc62-496d-ad3c-c6a795a33c27/analystreport

Also read the Activity Profile: Iranian MOIS operators opportunistically deploy limited-impact wiper in response to Israel-Hamas war Threat Analytics report: https://security.microsoft.com/threatanalytics3/c6674205-df28-453a-9e42-0010b7979bdd/overview?tid4b2462a4-bbee-495a-a0e1-f23ae524cc9c
